executions.label: Scan the snapshot (secrets, dependencies, code rules, configuration)
executions.command:
bash <<'CC_SCAN'
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/cc-sec/venv/bin:/opt/cc-sec/bin:$PATH SEMGREP_ENABLE_VERSION_CHECK=0 SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY=/opt/cc-sec/osv-db
rm -rf /cc-out /work/app && mkdir -p /cc-out /work/app
tar xzf /in/snapshot.tgz -C /work/app --no-same-owner
cd /work/app
timeout 300 gitleaks detect --no-git --source /work/app --report-format json --report-path /cc-out/gitleaks.json --exit-code 0 > /cc-out/gitleaks.log 2>&1; echo $? > /cc-out/gitleaks.exit
timeout 600 semgrep scan --metrics=off --disable-version-check --config /cc-rules/javascript.yml --config /cc-rules/python.yml --json --output /cc-out/semgrep.json --timeout 30 --max-target-bytes 1000000 /work/app > /cc-out/semgrep.log 2>&1; echo $? > /cc-out/semgrep.exit
timeout 300 osv-scanner scan --experimental-offline --format json --output /cc-out/osv.json -r /work/app > /cc-out/osv.log 2>&1; echo $? > /cc-out/osv.exit
timeout 300 trivy config --quiet --skip-version-check --skip-check-update --cache-dir /opt/cc-sec/trivy-cache -f json -o /cc-out/trivy.json /work/app > /cc-out/trivy.log 2>&1; echo $? > /cc-out/trivy.exit
for t in gitleaks semgrep osv trivy; do printf '%s=%s ' "$t" "$(cat /cc-out/$t.exit)"; done; echo
CC_SCAN

issues.message: 8 endpoints are protected by requireUser, requireRole, but no authentication mechanism was identified.
The security model says no authentication was found while endpoints are protected.

limitations: Static rules find known patterns only; a clean scan is not proof that the code is secure.
Code patterns, including traced injection paths, stay suspected until a runtime proof (Round 2) or a review confirms them.
The project analysis contradicts itself; checks that rely on it are inconclusive (lanes: auth, access_control).
Vulnerability data from the OSV database downloaded 2026-10-14T12:04:03Z; advisories published later are not included.
Configuration that depends on where the app is deployed (headers added by a proxy, cookie defaults) is reported as suspected.
